newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sold less barley than planned to Saudi - ONIC.
newsitem.headline: France sold less barley than planned to Saudi - ONIC.

text.p: France's grain office head linked a downwards revision in ONIC's forecast of French barley exports outside the European Union in new 1996/97 season to lower than expected sales of French wheat to Saudi Arabia.
ONIC director-general Alain Moulinier also said on Wednesday Saudi Arabia may shop again for barley to cover its import requirements for the February-June period.

"We have lowered our target for barley sales to non-EU countries because the last three deals clinched with Saudi Arabia since May were mostly covered, for the European share, with German barley," Moulinier told a monthly news conference.
In its November report released ahead of the conference ONIC cut its target for barley exports to non-EU countries to 1.2 million tonnes from last month's target of 1.5 million tonnes.
This would still represent a jump from the 221,000 tonnes exported to non-EU countries in 1995/96.
Last September exporters sold 1.4 million tonnes of feed barley to Saudi Arabia. The EU, with a freight and supply advantage over other origins, was expected to provide the bulk of the sale.

A large part of the EU share was initially covered with German intervention barley. France had hoped to participate in the contract through open-market barley sales, but French barley prices were less competitive than British and German. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
